defect_reproduction.exact_exception: LifecycleTelemetryOutboxError: canonical lifecycle payload build failed for order_submitted (raised from _emit_lifecycle_telemetry inside the PaperExecutionAlgorithm event sink, after _commit_fill).
defect_reproduction.source_cause: A committed paper fill was published as five separately-admitted lifecycle events (risk_evaluation, order_submitted, order_accepted, fill, position_snapshot). Any build/persistence failure after the first admission left a partial chain, and the exception propagated out of execute() into SignalConsumer, which DLQ'd the signal as unexpected_error and left its execution fence in_progress. A reclaimed copy then only produced execution_in_progress_elsewhere noop, so the ledger (fill_count 2, flat) and the Telemetry projection (fill 1, short 1) diverged permanently.
defect_reproduction.caveat: The runtime stderr of the original hosted failure was not available in the saved evidence; the concrete trigger on the host (transient build failure vs process interruption after risk_evaluation admission) is inferred from the saved outbox (chain tj_f1ec4785 stops at risk_evaluation seq 3, then noop events seq 4-6) and the in_progress fence. Both triggers are covered by the fix and by tests.

paper_runtime.py: Committed-fill lifecycle chain (risk, order_submitted, order_accepted, fill, position_snapshot) is staged and admitted in ONE atomic outbox write (LifecycleTelemetryOutbox.admit_many) with an idempotency batch id; no partial chain is possible.

Each committed fill is staged in the existing per-binding paper performance ledger (pending_fill_publications, written before the sink runs, same precedent as pending_performance_pair) and acknowledged only after durable admission.

PaperRuntimeService._on_order_event no longer lets a publication failure escape after the ledger committed (no DLQ, fence completes, no second trade); the staged fill is replayed on the next drain/restart with the original identities (event_id, broker_order_id, trade_episode_id, envelope) and deterministic payloads (position values come from the committed fill, created_at from the fill).
runtime_summary.py: pnl/drawdown snapshots carry the authoritative ledger fill_count; when it exceeds the fill events projected, fill-derived positions are withheld (positions=[], position_count=null, positions_status=unavailable, reason fill_event_gap) instead of presenting a stale open position. Missing pnl/drawdown/sharpe stay absent, never zero.
unchanged: signal idempotency and execution fence semantics (signal_consumer.py untouched)

historical_recovery_limitations.treatment: Truthful-unavailable: after this release the hosted summary receives pnl/drawdown snapshots with ledger fill_count=2 versus 1 projected fill and reports positions unavailable (fill_event_gap) instead of short 1. No fill/position event is forged, the signal is not re-executed and its in_progress fence is not cleared.
historical_recovery_limitations.not_recoverable_by_this_change: The historical ledger has no pending_fill_publications record (it predates this change), so the missing order_submitted/order_accepted/fill/position_snapshot events for that close cannot be replayed from durable state; any causal proof for them stays absent. Root handles hosted readback after delivery.
historical_recovery_limitations.residual_window: The fill is committed (ledger write) and then staged (second local write) before publication; a crash between those two local writes still leaves an unreplayable fill, but the projection fill_event_gap treatment keeps the summary truthful in that case.
